title: Tilsiter Chicken Bites with Honey-Dijon Glaze
summary: Golden chicken bites tossed in a tangy-sweet honey-Dijon pan glaze, topped with melted Tilsiter, and served with fire-roasted vegetables.
sourceNote: A protein-forward weeknight chicken dinner made more interesting with nutty Tilsiter, a sharp honey-Dijon glaze, and a generous helping of roasted vegetables.

ingredients.note: cut into roughly 1-inch chunks; kitchen shears work well
such as PuraVida; keep frozen until roasting
divided between two batches of chicken

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Spread 6 cups frozen fire-roasted Primavera vegetables in a single layer on a large sheet pan. Because the vegetables are already coated in avocado oil, do not add more unless the package directions call for it. Roast for 18–25 minutes, stirring once, until hot with browned edges rather than soft and steamy.

While the vegetables roast at 425°F, cut 1½ lb chicken breasts into roughly 1-inch chunks with a knife or kitchen shears. Keep the pieces similar in size. Pat dry and toss with ¾ tsp kosher salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp dried thyme, and ½ tsp black pepper. No breading is needed.

Heat half of the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the chicken in a single layer without crowding. Leave undisturbed for 2–3 minutes to brown, then turn occasionally until cooked through, about 6–9 minutes total. Check several of the largest pieces for an internal temperature of 165°F. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and chicken, adjusting the heat to keep the browned bits from burning.

With the cooked chicken removed, add ½ cup chicken broth, 1½ tbsp Dijon mustard, 2 tsp honey, and the optional 1 tsp apple cider vinegar to the skillet. Scrape up the browned bits and simmer for 2–4 minutes, stirring, until slightly reduced and lightly coating a spoon. Taste and adjust with black pepper.

Return the cooked chicken bites to the skillet and toss briefly in the honey-Dijon glaze. Scatter 3 oz shredded Tilsiter over the chicken, reduce the heat to low, and cover for 1–2 minutes, just until the cheese melts. For an unglazed portion, keep some cooked chicken separate before tossing and melt its share of cheese separately.
Divide the cheesy honey-Dijon chicken bites among 3 plates and serve with the roasted Primavera vegetables. Spoon any remaining pan glaze over the vegetables if desired.
